messages:
maya: Alan hit intermittent stream cutoff + 401 when using our hosted endpoint, asking for a minimal curl repro so we can validate headers/auth rotation. He attached a curl snippet and a truncated response.

alan-cust: here's what I'm running locally, happens ~30s into the stream: 
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...\" 
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" 
  -H \"Connection: keep-alive\" 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream
```

maya: good, can you add `-H \"X-Request-Id: <req-id>\"` and run with `-v --no-buffer`? we need the full handshake headers + the auth header TTL. also prefer `--http1.1` if you're behind an enterprise proxy.

alan-cust: adding X-Request-Id now, got req-id: req_20280301_alan_01. output pasted below (truncated):
```
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (1.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/chat/stream HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> User-Agent: curl/7.79.1
> Accept: text/event-stream
> Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...
> X-Request-Id: req_20280301_alan_01
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: text/event-stream
< cache-control: no-cache
< x-request-id: req_20280301_alan_01
< 
data: {"token":"partial"}
...stream continues for ~28s
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< x-request-id: req_20280301_alan_01
< www-authenticate: Bearer realm=\"tokens\", error=\"expired_token\"
```

jonah: thanks — that `www-authenticate` header shows token expiry. two quick asks: (1) does the client proactively refresh tokens mid-stream? (2) can you reproduce with a short-lived token we mint here so we can control TTL?

alan-cust: client refreshes on 25s, but stream keeps open. i'll try a server-provided short token.

sophie: for reproduction we usually ask for: full curl with `-v --no-buffer --http1.1 -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -H \"X-Request-Id: <id>\"`, and additionally capture `curl --trace-ascii debug.txt` so we can see chunk boundaries. example minimal command: 
```
curl -v --no-buffer --http1.1 --trace-ascii debug.txt \\n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <short-token>" \\n  -H "X-Request-Id: repro_alanshort_01" \\n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream
```

sophie: also include `--cookie \"session=...\"` if you reproduce auth via signed cookies; proxy chain can rewrite `Connection` and chunking. :mag:  

maya: i'll open a debug bundle request on the backend side for req_id=req_20280301_alan_01 and link logs + wire traces. support-bot: please create bundle.

support-bot: Debug bundle ticket created: DBG-3487. Backend logs pinned for req_20280301_alan_01, trace_id=trace_0a7f3e, allocated to eng-runtime. Please attach curl debug.txt and any client-side logs.

alan-cust: attached debug.txt, ran the exact command. debug shows chunk sizes, then a `RST_STREAM` from upstream before 401 in the tcp dump. pasting small excerpt: 
```
> GET /v1/chat/stream HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
chunked body: 16
...data...
* Received RST_STREAM, code 11
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
```

jonah: RST_STREAM code 11 = INTERNAL_ERROR on HTTP2. that plus 401 indicates token middleware closed connection while token refresh in-flight. can you confirm if your client does an in-place refresh vs opening new connection? the recommended pattern: if token refresh needed, reopen stream after refresh; do not try to swap the Authorization header mid-connection.

alan-cust: client tries to swap header in-place (we mutate the request object). okay i'll switch to closing+reopen and retest.

sophie: one more validation step for us: reproduce with `--http1.1` and without to confirm it's protocol-specific. if issue only on http2, we'll add a fallback in our routing. also include `curl -I` before streaming to confirm initial handshake TTL header `x-token-ttl` if your auth service sets it.

maya: next actions: (1) alan to retest with close+reopen flow + share new req-id, debug.txt; (2) eng-runtime to watch DBG-3487 traces for trace_0a7f3e and check whether token refresh events correlate with RST_STREAM; (3) doc update suggested: add a note in our streaming guide to avoid swapping Authorization mid-stream. :memo: 

alan-cust: will do the close+reopen test and post results here later today. thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
